$comment: The reasons a verdict lists (agentcake/detect/verdict_text.py fills them in). Each has the layer it belongs to, its evidence grade (env_rules.json legend: measured, project-claim, source, inferred) its English text (what it means) and, when it has one, its detail (what was seen, in technical words: the second line under the text); {placeholders} in both are filled from the reason's facts, which the verdict keeps so that a reason is worded anew each time it is shown (verdict_text.words: facts named half, method, other_method, basis, signals, marker and signature name a phrase of this file, agent_markers.json or webbotauth.json), {product} is the product name (product.json) and $missing stands in for a fact that is not known. tone is how the interface marks it (agent, human or none: a fact for neither). Layers are the interface's (web/src/data/schema/session.schema.json: name, verify, environment, behavior) plus exclusion (rule 0) and weak (weak signals). An environment rule's hit is listed under the rule's own id with the rule's title and detail (env_rules.json); a Web Bot Auth result's own words come from webbotauth.json and fill {signature} and {signature_detail}; an agent product's indicator fills {marker} and {marker_detail} from agent_markers.json. Interface text (English only; Human / Agent / Mixed / Not sure / Bot).

behavior_basis.rules_unnamed: enough of the clicks and typing look like an agent's
behavior_basis.active_move_rate: the pointer moves too rarely for a human hand
behavior_basis.typing_cadence: the typing rhythm doesn't vary the way a human's does
behavior_basis.fast_arrivals: most pointer movements don't slow down near the click target, unlike a human hand

behavior_kinds.approach: how the pointer approaches each click
behavior_kinds.integrity: how the input events are made
behavior_kinds.page: activity while the page has no focus

methods.automation-trace: the tool's own trace in the page

exclude.prefetch.text: The Server half of page {page} doesn't count.
exclude.prefetch.detail: The page was requested as a {purpose}: its request carried Sec-Purpose: {purpose}.

exclude.never-shown.text: Page {page} was prepared in advance but never shown, so it doesn't count.
exclude.never-shown.detail: The browser prerendered it and never showed it.

exclude.all.text: Not a visit: every page was prepared in advance but never shown.
exclude.all.detail: Every page was prerendered and never shown.

name.ua.detail: The User-Agent of {half} names {name}, listed as {kind_label}.

name.ua-generic.text: {name} is a tool anyone can run. No agent product is named.

name.ua-conflict.text: It gives several product names at once, so none of them counts.

name.ua-hint.text: The browser's identification looks forged or malformed. This is weak evidence.

name.platform.text: The browser reports the same platform as {name}.

name.signer.text: The request names {signer}, a signer for {name}.

name.unknown-signer.text: The request names a signer this release doesn't know.
name.unknown-signer.detail: Signature-Agent on {half}: {signer}, which isn't among the bundled signers.

name.disagree.text: The names it gives disagree, so the visit gets no name.

name.signer-mismatch.text: It names one signer but is signed by another.

name.outranked.text: Shown as {name} because its naming method takes priority.

name.from-trace.detail: This trace belongs to {name}, but a product's trace can change when it updates.

verify.signature-forged.text: It claims to be {name}, but its signature doesn't verify. That's impersonation, so the visit gets no name.

verify.signature-proxy.text: The signature couldn't be verified. A proxy in front of your site may have changed the request, so this isn't impersonation.
verify.signature-proxy.detail: {signature_detail} The signature covers {components}, which a proxy in front of the site may rewrite.

verify.ip-range.text: Verified: the address is one {operator} publishes for {name}.

verify.ip-agent-range.text: The address is one {operator} publishes for its agents.

verify.ip-bot-range.text: The address is one {operator} publishes for its crawlers, but the visitor gives no name.

verify.ip-mismatch.text: It claims to be {name}, but the address isn't one {operator} publishes for it. That's impersonation, so the visit gets no name.

verify.rdns-mismatch.text: It claims to be {name}, but its address doesn't confirm that. That's impersonation, so the visit gets no name.

verify.no-range.text: {product} can't verify {name}, so the name is self-reported.
verify.no-range.detail: {name} publishes no address range or key that {product} can check.

verify.local.text: In local mode, names are self-reported.
verify.local.detail: Every visit comes from 127.0.0.1, so there's no verification layer.

verify.no-address.text: Names are self-reported because the visitor's address wasn't available.
verify.no-address.detail: The check against the published ranges didn't run.

env.automated.text: The browser shows signs of automation, but not which tool. It may be an AI tool working for a human, or a script.
env.automated.detail: Automation markers are present, but none of them names the tool.

env.cloud-browser.text: It runs in a cloud browser that doesn't say who operates it.

env.extension-unnamed.text: A browser extension acted on this page, but nothing shows which one.

env.soft-alone.text: The only signs come from DevTools, privacy tools, or similar features that humans also use. These aren't enough on their own.

behavior.agent.text: The session's behavior looks like an agent's.

behavior.turns.text: A human and an agent took turns.

behavior.turns-runs.text: A human and an agent took turns.

behavior.human.text: The session's behavior looks like a human's.

behavior.one-kind.text: Only one kind of behavior looks like an agent's. That isn't enough to call it an agent.
behavior.one-kind.detail: Behavior model: the only agent-like evidence is {kind}. Calling it an agent takes two independent kinds.

behavior.unsure.text: The behavior model can't tell whether the session is a human's or an agent's.

behavior.indicator.text: {marker}, so the actions in that time are the agent's.

behavior.indicator-tail.text: {marker}, so the actions until {until} are the agent's.
behavior.indicator-tail.detail: {marker_detail} It stays on for a few seconds after the agent's last action, so later actions are judged by their behavior.

behavior.handoff.text: The {to} took over from the {from} at {at}.

behavior.short-run.text: A short run by the {who} doesn't count as the {who} taking part.
behavior.short-run.detail: The {who} run has {n} actions in {span} s.

behavior.overruled.text: The behavior model judged the session human, but that doesn't outweigh the signs of automation.

behavior.assistive.text: The navigation looks like an assistive tool's, so the behavior model's agent finding isn't trusted.
behavior.assistive.detail: The visitor navigates with the keyboard and no pointer, as assistive tools do.

behavior.local-agent.text: Possibly an agent on the visitor's own computer: only the behavior points to an agent.
behavior.local-agent.detail: There's no agent trace in the page or the browser.

behavior.too-little-data.text: The behavior model doesn't judge the session because there are too few actions.
behavior.too-little-data.detail: The session has {n} actions; the model needs {min}.

behavior.touch.text: This visit came from a phone or tablet, so the behavior model isn't used.

behavior.not-run-bot.text: This is a listed bot, known by name, so the behavior model doesn't run.

crawler.like.text: The visit looks like a crawler's. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.timezone-country.text: The browser's time zone isn't used in the country of its address. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.language-country.text: None of the browser's language settings specifies the country linked to its address. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.same-address.text: {n} sessions came from this address within {hours} h. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.header-order.text: The requests don't match the browser they claim to come from. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.
weak.header-order.detail: The User-Agent says {browser}, but cake.js's requests list their headers in an order {browser} doesn't use: {order}.

weak.display-change.text: The screen changed during the session. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.window-jump.text: The window jumped across the screen without changing size. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.

weak.rhythm-pauses.text: Pauses before actions can suggest an AI examining the page before it acts. This weak signal doesn't change the verdict.
weak.rhythm-pauses.detail: {pct}% of the steps came after at least {seconds} s without input.
